chemistry.org-alc-explain-items.0007.all: Same homologous series; same functional group (-OH), which determines the reactions.

chemistry.org-alc-mcq-facts.0011.all: it is a continuous process giving pure ethanol

chemistry.org-alc2-recall-facts.0008.all: Continuous process / faster / produces pure (not dilute) ethanol.

chemistry.org-alk-explain-items.0005.all: Alkanes are saturated (only C-C single bonds), no C=C for addition; substitution with bromine needs UV light.

chemistry.org-crude-describe-items.0003.all: Sulfur impurities in fuel burn to SO2; SO2 dissolves in rainwater / reacts with water and oxygen; forms sulfuric (sulfurous) acid, lowering pH of rain.

chemistry.org-crude-explain-items.0003.all: Colourless, odourless toxic gas; combines with haemoglobin, reducing the blood's capacity to carry oxygen.

chemistry.org-ene-describe-items.0011.all: Each successive member differs by CH2.

chemistry.org-est-practical-items.0001.all: Mix ethanol and ethanoic acid in a test tube; add a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst; warm in a hot water bath; pour into sodium carbonate solution/water and smell the fruity ester.

chemistry.org-intro-explain-items.0012.all: Combustion breaks up the whole molecule (all bonds) forming CO2 and H2O; no atom is simply replaced (substitution) and no atoms are added across a double bond (addition) - it is oxidation.

chemistry.org-poly-explain-items.0009.all: Condensation polymerisation needs each monomer to react at both ends; ester link forms between -COOH and -OH, so need a dicarboxylic acid + diol (or a hydroxy-acid), eliminating water.

chemistry.periodic-explain-items.0009.all: Blue = alkaline solution (pH ~8-10); metal oxides are basic, so the element is a metal.

chemistry.periodic-mcq-facts.0003.all: they have the same number of outer electrons

chemistry.polymers-eq.0016.ii: Polyester (condensation polymer) can be hydrolysed / is biodegradable, whereas poly(ethene) is inert (strong C-C bonds) and non-biodegradable.

chemistry.polymers-recall.0003.c: Water pipes / window frames / cable insulation

chemistry.rates-explain-items.0006.all: Particles closer together / more particles per unit volume; more frequent collisions (more successful collisions per second).

chemistry.rates-extended-items.0012.all: Higher pressure: more particles per volume, more frequent collisions. Higher temperature: particles have more kinetic energy, more collisions with energy >= Ea, more frequent. Not maximum: high pressure is expensive (equipment, energy) and dangerous; high temperature costs energy and may lower equilibrium yield (exothermic), so compromise conditions used.
